cases.question: According to Python itertools.groupby documentation, does it group equal keys anywhere in the input or only consecutive runs, and how should input be prepared to collect all equal keys together?
cases.query: Python itertools.groupby consecutive groups sorted same key documentation
gold_aspects: groupby creates groups for consecutive runs of equal keys; it does not aggregate equal keys globally regardless of input order.
To collect all items of each key together, input should be sorted/grouped on the same key function before groupby; groupby does not perform sorting itself.
primary_quote: Make an iterator that returns consecutive keys and groups from the iterable.
sorted on the same key function.
cases.source_date_or_viewed_date: Viewed 2026-11-18; page header Python 3.15.2 documentation; section itertools.groupby, lines279-280 in browser text.
evaluation_notes: A statement that SQL GROUP BY and itertools.groupby group irrespective of input order is false.
A correct example without the general consecutive-run rule is not sufficient support for a general claim.
Do not call sorting mandatory for every possible use: consecutive grouping is valid without prior sorting; sorting is for collecting all equal keys.

cases.question: По официальной документации Python Path.resolve: что происходит с несуществующим остатком пути при strict=False, чем отличается strict=True и устраняет ли resolve компоненты '..'?
cases.query: Python pathlib Path.resolve strict False nonexistent remainder strict True documentation
gold_aspects: При strict=False путь разрешается настолько далеко, насколько возможно; оставшаяся часть добавляется без проверки её существования.
При strict=True несуществующий путь приводит к OSError; FileNotFoundError допустим как конкретный подкласс для отсутствующего пути, но не как универсальный тип всех ошибок resolve.
Path.resolve устраняет компоненты '..' (а также делает путь абсолютным и разрешает симлинки; последние два свойства не обязательные аспекты данного вопроса).
primary_quote: the path is resolved as far as possible
appended without checking whether it exists.
cases.source_date_or_viewed_date: Viewed 2026-11-18; page header Python 3.15.2 documentation; section Path.resolve, lines749-767 in browser text.
evaluation_notes: Question does not require symlink-loop behavior; do not add version-dependent universal RuntimeError claims.
A claim that strict=False proves the returned path exists is false.
Keep strict mode and missing-path condition attached to the exception claim; general filesystem background does not satisfy it.

cases.question: Верно ли, что copy.copy в Python рекурсивно копирует вложенные изменяемые объекты и поэтому изолирует их от оригинала? Чем это отличается от copy.deepcopy?
cases.query: Python copy.copy shallow copy nested mutable objects references deepcopy documentation
gold_aspects: False premise: shallow copy creates a new outer compound object but inserts references to contained original objects, so nested mutable objects can remain shared.
Deep copy recursively copies contained objects, subject to module/type/custom-copy behavior; do not claim universal isolation of every possible object.
primary_quote: A shallow copy constructs a new compound object
inserts references into it to the objects found in the original.
cases.source_date_or_viewed_date: Viewed2026-11-18, Python3.12.16 docs, pageupdated2026-10-26; shallow/deep distinction lines25-39.
evaluation_notes: Must reject the stated shallow-copy premise explicitly or give an unambiguously contradictory accurate explanation.
A lone specific list example does not establish the general copy contract without own general-rule evidence.
No unqualified guarantee that deepcopy copies modules/files/functions or ensures universal isolation.
